item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 040538
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Sep 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on Hurricane Marie, located several hundred miles west-
southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico early next week. Gradual development is possible, and the
system could become a tropical depression around the middle of next
week while it moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, likely
remaining well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Blake

--------------------

DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was
located near latitude 20.4 North, longitude 139.3 West. Karina is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected to continue for the next couple of days.

Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Gradual weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours,
although Karina is expected to remain a hurricane during the next
day or two.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Thu Sep 03 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 040853
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 PM HST Thu Sep 03 2026

The eye of Karina has become a little less well-defined over the 
past several hours with some breaks in the eyewall evident in 
satellite imagery.  The coldest cloud tops are around -60 deg C 
with more deep convection prevalent over the eastern semicircle.  
Subjective Dvorak classifications from TAFB have decreased 
somewhat, as have most of the objective intensity estimates from 
UW-CIMSS.  The advisory intensity is reduced only slightly to 85 
kt, which is close to the latest SATCON value from UW-CIMSS. 

The hurricane continues moving west-northwestward with a motion 
estimate of 285/8 kt.  Karina should continue this general motion 
during the next day or two while it is situated on the southern 
side of a mid-level ridge.  In 48 hours, a mid-level cyclone to the 
north of Hawaii is likely to cause a turn toward the northwest.  By 
96 hours, Karina should be a shallow weakening system and it will 
probably turn leftward while interacting with the circulation of 
Hurricane Lowell.  The official track forecast is very close to the 
previous NHC prediction and follows the corrected model consensus 
guidance.

Water vapor imagery shows Karina approaching an area of drier 
mid-level air which is likely to begin eroding the hurricane within 
the next day or so.  The SHIPS model output shows a significant 
increase in vertical wind shear commencing in about 36 hours.  
Although SSTs along Karina's path are not expected to cool that 
much more during the next few days, the hostile atmospheric 
moisture and shear are likely to cause Karina to weaken.  The 
system should become a post-tropical cyclone early next week, and 
dissipate soon thereafter.

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...MARIE COULD STRENGTHEN SOME MORE TODAY... As of 2:00 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 the center of Marie was located near 19.9, -117.1 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 972 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 100 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Marie Public Advisory Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 040854
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026
 
...MARIE COULD STRENGTHEN SOME MORE TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.9N 117.1W
ABOUT 505 MI...815 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...972 MB...28.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 19.9 North, longitude 117.1 West.  Marie is moving
toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and a gradual turn 
toward the northwest is expected within the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Some strengthening is possible today, but a slow weakening 
trend is expected to begin on Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).  The Mexican Navy Weather station on Clarion Island 
recently reported sustained winds of 51 mph (81 km/h) and a wind 
gust to 70 mph (112 km/h). 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 972 mb (28.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for
the next few days and are expected to spread northward to Southern
California through the weekend.  These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please
consult products from your local weather office.  A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 040855
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026

Marie has numerous bands of deep convection in its circulation, but 
the inner core is still not very well defined with a somewhat 
ragged-looking eye.  The system has a prominent upper-level outflow 
pattern, indicative of a low-shear environment.  Remotely-sensed 
intensity estimates are generally in the range of 80-90 kt, and the 
current intensity estimate is kept at 85 kt for this advisory.

The hurricane is moving west-northwestward, or around 295/8 kt, on 
the southwestern periphery of a mid-tropospheric ridge.  Global 
models depict a 500-mb trough swinging into California in a couple 
of days.  This evolution is likely to result in Marie turning 
toward the northwest in 36 hours or so.  Later in the forecast 
period, the weakening cyclone should move more with the low- to 
mid-level environmental flow and remain well offshore over the 
eastern Pacific.  The official track forecast is nudged a bit to 
the right of the previous one in 3-5 days, toward the latest Google 
DeepMind and corrected consensus, HCCA, guidance.

Marie is expected to remain in an environment of low vertical wind 
shear for the next several days.  However SSTs are forecast to 
decrease, and the system should be encounter a drier low- to 
mid-level air mass by 48 hours.  Some strengthening is forecast 
while the hurricane remains in a conducive atmospheric and oceanic 
environment through tonight.  Later, a weakening trend is likely as 
Marie encounters less favorable conditions.  The official forecast 
is close to the intensity model consensus.
